We observe that in the Petitions filed by the SPDs where claims under Change in Law were adjudicated, the Commission has directed SPDs to make available to SECI/ Discoms all relevant documents exhibiting clear and one to one correlation between the projects and the supply of goods or services, duly supported by the relevant invoices and Auditor’s Certificate. SECI/ Discoms were further directed to reconcile the claims for Change in Law on receipt of the relevant documents and pay the amount so claimed to SPDs. It was also held that SECI is liable to pay to SPDs which is not conditional upon the payment to be made by the Discoms to SECI. However, SECI is eligible to claim the same from the Discoms on ‘back to back’ basis. The claim was directed to be paid within sixty days of the date of respective orders or from the date of submission of claims by SPDs whichever was later failing which it will attract late payment surcharge as provided under PPAs/PSAs.
